data.body:
═══ THE SAME ROOT CAUSE WAS BREAKING FOUR MORE PER-CALL MODEL CHOICES, ALL IN PLAN-REVIEW ═══

Committed as **2e17171e5c** (`b690: honour a step's declared model at the runner`), Change-Id
`Id942221c950b8c38eb09295d634cb0a37f581653`, on top of 44d9250ea. NOT pushed yet — full unit suite
re-running first. Then I audited the blast radius of the fix, and it is wider than this ticket's
title. Recording it because it changes gate behaviour and the operator should decide, not me.

**MEASURED: of 22 `RunRequest` construction sites under `src/rebar`, FOUR deliberately pass a
config DIFFERENT from the one their runner was built with — and all four were therefore silently
ineffective.** Every one is in plan-review:
 * `plan_review/xcheck.py:199` (contradiction sub-call) — `runner_sel = runner or get_runner(cfg)`
   then `config=_verifier_cfg(cfg)`.
 * `plan_review/xcheck.py:337` (comment-trail sub-call) — same shape.
 * `plan_review/__init__.py:164` (novelty sub-call) — `config=replace(_verifier_cfg(cfg),
   temperature=0.0)`.
 * `plan_review/prerequisites.py:228` — `call_cfg = dataclasses.replace(cfg, model=model)`.

So `_verifier_cfg` — the whole point of `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL`, "a focused yes/no verification is
a decisive, non-open-ended judgement, so a cheaper/faster model is sufficient" — has been building a
verifier config that the runner then ignored. Three Pass-2 sub-calls that were meant to run on the
cheaper decisive model have in fact been running on the frontier model.

**AND THE FOURTH IS WORSE THAN A MISSED OPTIMISATION — IT MADE A PROVENANCE RECORD UNTRUE.**
`prerequisites.py` implements a SIZE-ESCALATION LADDER: on a context-limit error it retries a bin on
a higher model (`ladder = sizing.models_at_or_above(model)`), and records the producing model per id
via `_from(model, …)`. Its own comment at `:202-204` states the requirement:

    # A ladder escalation re-runs a bin on a HIGHER model, so the producing model is not always
    # cfg.model; emit_indeterminate must report what actually ran, not what was configured
    # (client report §4).

Both halves of that were broken by the same discard. The escalation never escalated — every rung ran
on `cfg.model` — and the record reported the model the code ASKED for rather than the one that ran,
which is precisely the failure that comment exists to prevent. A client report (§4) is behind it.

**WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX: it is doing more than wiring five code-review declarations. It makes
`_verifier_cfg`, the novelty pass's greedy verifier config, and the prerequisite ladder all take
effect for the first time.** That is the designed behaviour in every case — no code changed its
intent, only its efficacy — but it IS a live behaviour change to the plan-review gate, which is the
gate that reviews the plans in this very epic:
 * three Pass-2 sub-calls move frontier → the verifier model (with no class table configured, opus →
   sonnet). Intended and cheaper; the risk to weigh is that a sub-call which only reached its
   current verdict BECAUSE it ran on opus may now decide differently.
 * the prerequisite ladder starts actually escalating on context-limit errors, which changes what a
   large plan's prerequisite pass does under pressure (previously it retried the same model and,
   presumably, hit the same limit).

**FLAGGING RATHER THAN DECIDING.** Per the epic's mandate I am not calling any of this out of scope,
and I have not narrowed the fix to code-review to avoid the change — narrowing would leave four known
defects in place, and the epic's mandate is to ship WITHOUT BUGS. But "plan-review verifier passes
change model" is an operator-visible consequence of a story titled for code-review, so it should be
an explicit decision. If the operator wants the plan-review consequences verified before this lands,
the natural shape is a sibling ticket under 061c that re-runs a plan review and a prerequisite-heavy
plan under the new behaviour and records the observed per-pass models — which the Step 0 attribution
now makes checkable, and which was impossible before this ticket.

**Not cited as a defect, deliberately:** `resolve_verifier_model`'s equality rule remains superseded
and callerless per the standing decision. The live thing here is `_verifier_cfg`, which has callers.
